evidence.observation: Plan says "`--physical-binding FILE` together with `--ontology-only` is refused as a usage error (exit 2)" and OB1 C4 says "the argument is refused at the CLI boundary when 0, negative, non-integer or above the ceiling (exit 2)". In src/gnd/cli.py lines 27-32 the code documents "64 (EX_USAGE): malformed invocation (argparse usage error). argparse's default ``SystemExit(2)`` would masquerade as \"vacuous population\" ... Do not \"fix\" this." src/gnd/exits.py:46 has EXIT_USAGE = 64.

concerns.recommendation: Change OB1-C4 and §2.1 to expect exit 64 (EXIT_USAGE). As written, C4 can pass only by breaking the project's band contract, which reserves exit 2 for 'vacuous'.
concerns.title: OB1-C4 and §2.1 expect exit 2 for usage errors; GND's usage exit is 64

evidence.location: Completion predicates item 1, lines 28-31; §2.1 line 146; §5 lines 234-236; D2 line 301
evidence.observation: Predicate 1: "`gnd export ossie MODEL --out OUT` behaves exactly as today when no new flag is given ... the three files are byte-identical to the baseline". §5: "Under D2 (a), a default run now writes five files. A caller whose `OUT.semantic_model.*` or `OUT.mapping.*` already exists gets exit 10 (collision) where today's run succeeded." D2 proposes (a).

concerns.recommendation: Make predicate 1 conditional on D2. Under (a), the predicate should say the three legacy files are byte-identical and the run also writes two new files. Without a new flag, the run behaves exactly as today only with --ontology-only. Otherwise the proposed default falsifies predicate 1.
concerns.title: Completion predicate 1 ('behaves exactly as today') cannot hold under the proposed D2(a) default

evidence.observation: Predicate 2: the Rmap "turns every model of the export census into a relational schema, or refuses it with a closed reason". D2: "(a) as requested, **provided** OB2's census shows the Rmap is total on every census model", with the stated cost "(a) a default run can newly fail (collision, or Rmap refusal) where it succeeded."

concerns.recommendation: Define 'total' for D2 as 'no census model is refused'. Separately, decide what an Rmap refusal does on the default path for models outside the census: degrade to listing in the GND extension or refuse the run. Without that rule, user models that export today can start failing by default.
concerns.title: D2(a) lets an Rmap refusal fail a default export that succeeds today; 'total' is ambiguous

evidence.location: Intro line 16; §1.2 lines 107-109; OB1 C2 line 212
evidence.observation: Line 16: "It makes the output size bound a parameter, so large models can export." §1.2: "The export source must be a standalone model of at most `MAX_MODEL_BYTES` (10 MiB) ... Whether the reporter's flattened model is under that cap is not known (D10)." In src/gnd/export/ossie.py:73 the read is stream.read(MAX_MODEL_BYTES + 1).

concerns.recommendation: Make the source cap an explicit decision, or add a predicate that bounds it. OB1 should state, with a measurement, the output-to-source expansion ratio for its generated C2 model. If the reporter's roughly 32 MiB case needs a source above 10 MiB, OB1 does not fix I1 for them, and no phase owns that gap.
concerns.title: The 10 MiB source cap may still block the 'large models' I1 targets; no decision owns it

evidence.location: §1.2 lines 103-106; OB1 C6 line 212; D3 line 302
evidence.observation: Plan cites only "`gnd import ossie` reads at most `MAX_BYTES` (`src/gnd/ossie_import.py:66`, `:78`)" and proposes `--max-input-bytes`. ossie_import.py has other fixed caps: _parse calls guard_yaml(data) with its default max_bytes=MAX_BYTES (line 86), _bounded_model raises "model-size" at MAX_BYTES (line 329), and the loss report is capped at 2 * MAX_BYTES (line 642).

concerns.recommendation: List every import-side cap that OB1-C6 must thread or deliberately keep: guard_yaml max_bytes, model-size and loss-size. State whether the re-imported model must still fit MAX_MODEL_BYTES. Otherwise C6 can fail on a cap the plan never names.
concerns.title: D3's --max-input-bytes names only the read cap; YAML guard, model-size and loss-size caps also bind

evidence.observation: "gets exit 10 (collision) where today's run succeeded. This is stated in the changelog". In src/gnd/exits.py:109 the code has EXIT_COLLISION = 11, and _cmd_export_ossie returns EXIT_COLLISION on FileExistsError.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the collision exit to 11 (EXIT_COLLISION) before it is copied into the changelog and specs.
concerns.title: Compatibility note gives the collision exit as 10; the code uses 11

evidence.location: §4 OB2 Ready column line 213; D5 line 305; §0 rule 6 line 69
evidence.observation: OB2 is "Blocked on D1, D5." D5 proposes "Halpin defaults ... settled by measurement in OB2." Rule 6 says variants "are settled by running both variants over the census". No metric is given for choosing between variants.

concerns.recommendation: Unblock OB2 from D5: OB2 implements both variants behind an internal switch and measures them, and D5 is ruled from the result before OB3. Name the decision metric, for example unmapped count, table count, or agreement with fixtures.
concerns.title: OB2 waits on D5, but D5 is to be settled by OB2's measurement, and that measurement has no metric

evidence.observation: §1.2 lists requirements for Relationship and Field ("`Field` requires `name` and `expression`") but not Dataset. In the vendored core-spec.json, Dataset has "required": ["name", "source"] (line 264), where source is "Reference to underlying physical table/view (database.schema.table) or query". §2.3 gives no rule for Dataset.source, Field.expression or Field.datatype on the Rmap path.

concerns.recommendation: Have OB2/OB3 fix deterministic values for Dataset.source and Field.expression when no physical schema exists, and say how value-type datatypes map to Field.datatype. Without those rules, OB3-C1 schema validity is undetermined and a fabricated physical source name could mislead consumers.
concerns.title: Rmap path has no rule for the required Dataset.source and Field.expression members

evidence.location: §2.3 Rmap bullet lines 166-173; OB2 C2 line 213
evidence.observation: "1:1 fact types are absorbed toward the mandatory side." The plan gives no rule when both sides or neither side is mandatory. "Reference modes become key columns" does not cover compound preferred reference schemes. The OB2 C2 corpus lists "compound uniqueness, functional grouping, 1:1, subtype absorbed and separate, objectification, reference modes, n-ary" and omits unary fact types and both-or-neither-mandatory 1:1.

concerns.recommendation: Add tie-break rules: 1:1 with both or neither side mandatory, unary fact types, compound preferred identification, and a fact type with several candidate uniqueness constraints to choose the primary from. Add those to the OB2-C2 fixture corpus, so that 'total, deterministic' can be tested.
concerns.title: Halpin Rmap rules leave determinism gaps (1:1 tie, unary, compound reference)

evidence.location: §1.1 I3 line 79; OB4 criteria line 215; D7 line 306
evidence.observation: I3 asks for "columns (`sql_type`, `targets`, `references`), `primary_key`, `roles` and `extension_roles`". OB4 C1 covers only "datasets, fields, PKs and relationships, each `references` becomes a relationship". No criterion says where `sql_type` goes (core-spec Field has `datatype`), what `extension_roles` does, or whether `unique_keys` (D4) come from the binding or the Rmap under --physical-binding.

concerns.recommendation: Give extension_roles and sql_type an owning OB4 criterion, or an explicit decision to defer them. State the source of unique_keys on the binding path.
concerns.title: I3's extension_roles and sql_type, and unique_keys under a binding, have no owning criterion

evidence.observation: "Unicode casefold plus removal of non-alphanumeric characters. Refuse a fact type whose roles collide after normalization." The plan names no Unicode normalization form (NFKC or NFC). It does not define 'alphanumeric', which could mean the ASCII set or Unicode categories such as str.isalnum. It does not say how a binding role name that normalizes to the empty string is handled.

concerns.recommendation: Pin the normalization: an NFKC form, the exact character class, and refusal of names that normalize to empty. Add hostile Unicode cases to the OB4 C6 test.
concerns.title: D8 role-name normalization is not precise enough to be deterministic across inputs

response.summary: I checked the §1.2 claims against src/gnd/export/ossie.py, src/gnd/ossie_import.py, src/gnd/commands/export.py and core-spec.json. The render_ossie refusal, the MAX_BYTES reuse, the import read cap and the unique_keys/Relationship/Field claims are accurate. Two problems block the plan. OB1-C4 and §2.1 expect usage errors to exit 2, but GND maps usage errors to 64. Completion predicate 1 ('behaves exactly as today') contradicts the proposed D2(a) default. The hardening gaps are: Rmap refusal on the default path, the unaddressed 10 MiB source cap, import caps outside the lines the plan cites, a wrong collision exit code, a D5/OB2 dependency cycle, required core-spec members (Dataset.source, Field.expression) with no Rmap rule, ambiguous Rmap rules, and I3 requests that no phase owns.

evidence.observation: OB2 is "Blocked on D1, D5," while D5 says its Rmap variants are "settled by measurement in OB2." The prerequisite decision depends on the phase it blocks.

concerns.recommendation: Put a bounded comparison before the OB2 spec gate, or make variant measurement an explicit early OB2 criterion with a subsequent decision gate.
concerns.title: D5 and OB2 form a decision cycle

evidence.observation: Predicate 1 says the command "behaves exactly as today when no new flag is given," but D2(a) makes five files the default. D2(b) is the fallback if the Rmap is not total, yet the proposed command surface has no flag to request relational output under that fallback.

concerns.recommendation: Choose a coherent default contract and specify the opt-in flag, its outputs and its acceptance checks if D2(b) remains possible.
concerns.title: The default-output fallback has no usable command path

evidence.observation: OB1 proposes "--max-input-bytes N" so "the large export round-trips through import." In the current importer, the read cap is only one limit: JSON decoding and YAML guarding retain 10 MiB caps, `_bounded_model` retains a 10 MiB result cap, and `load_model_bytes` parses under `MAX_MODEL_BYTES`.

concerns.recommendation: Define which import, parse and restored-model limits the new flag changes, and test a bundle that exceeds 10 MiB at each relevant boundary.
concerns.title: The import flag alone cannot establish large-bundle round trips

evidence.observation: The rules say "Each fact type with a compound uniqueness constraint gets its own table" and "Fact types whose role is functional on an entity are grouped into that entity's table." A binary fact with both a single-role uniqueness and a compound uniqueness satisfies both rules.

concerns.recommendation: State precedence or narrower eligibility for these placements and include a fixture with both uniqueness constraints.
concerns.title: Two Rmap placement rules can assign the same fact to different tables

evidence.observation: I3 places `references` among column members, while OB4-C1 says "each `references` becomes a relationship." The external check expects "relationships equal the DDL foreign keys." A two-column foreign key would become two relationships unless the binding can group its columns into one reference.

concerns.recommendation: Specify a composite-reference representation and require one ordered relationship per foreign key, with a composite-key fixture.
concerns.title: Column-level references do not represent composite foreign keys

evidence.observation: D6 requires "Same output with or without a population," while also retaining "the existing loss-report refusal." The loss report changes when a population is present; the planned mapping also carries model identity, which includes population content in the current implementation.

concerns.recommendation: Limit the equality claim to specified structural portions, and state the expected differences in the loss report, identity and mapping bytes.
concerns.title: Population-independent output conflicts with the planned metadata

evidence.observation: The Rmap says "1:1 fact types are absorbed toward the mandatory side," but gives no direction when both roles are mandatory or neither is mandatory. OB2-C2 only names "1:1" as a fixture category.

concerns.recommendation: Define a deterministic rule or closed refusal for both cases and add distinguishing fixtures.
concerns.title: One-to-one absorption has undefined cases

evidence.observation: The key rule says "The primary uniqueness becomes `primary_key`. Every other confirmed alethic uniqueness over one table's columns becomes a `unique_keys` entry," but does not say which uniqueness is primary when a table has multiple candidate keys.

concerns.recommendation: Specify key selection and tie-breaking from model semantics, with a fixture containing multiple candidate keys.
concerns.title: Primary-key selection is undefined for multiple candidate keys

response.summary: The baseline claims checked against the named source files hold, but phase dependencies and several output rules leave claimed behavior unprovable or contradictory.

evidence.observation: Predicate 1 requires that `gnd export ossie MODEL --out OUT` behaves exactly as today when no new flag is given (writing three files), but D2(a) proposes 'five files by default' with an opt-out flag.

concerns.recommendation: Condition Predicate 1 on D2(b) or update it to reflect the five-file default if D2(a) is chosen.

concerns.recommendation: Provide a deterministic tie-breaker for 1:1 absorption when mandatory constraints are symmetrical.

evidence.observation: Issue 3 requests the binding to supply 'columns (sql_type, targets, references), primary_key, roles and extension_roles'. OB4 C1 only requires 'a valid binding replaces datasets, fields, PKs and relationships', failing to own sql_type, targets, roles, and extension_roles.

evidence.observation: Section 2.3 requires listing 'Unrepresentable constructs (mandatory and NOT NULL, value constraints, frequency, ring, subset, exclusion, derivations, deontic rules)'. OB3 C3 only states 'every fact type is mapped or listed', omitting the unrepresentable constraints.

concerns.recommendation: Update OB3 criteria to explicitly verify the listing of all unrepresentable constructs, not just fact types.
concerns.title: Issue 2 requirement to list unrepresentable constructs is not fully owned by OB3

evidence.observation: Phase OB1 is marked as 'Ready: draft spec. Needs D3 only.' However, D3 determines the ceiling for the output bound and whether import gets a matching flag, meaning OB1 cannot be fully specified until D3 is ruled.

concerns.recommendation: Mark OB1 as blocked on D3 and refrain from finalizing its specification until the decision is ruled.

response.summary: Found blocking concerns regarding unfalsifiable predicates, ambiguous Rmap rules, and unowned requests from the source issues.

evidence.observation: The plan states: "A caller whose `OUT.semantic_model.*` or `OUT.mapping.*` already exists gets exit 10 (collision) where today's run succeeded." In the code this plan is checked against, the collision band is EXIT_COLLISION = 11 (src/gnd/exits.py:109, "EXIT_COLLISION = 11  # an unmanaged file blocked a write; nothing was destroyed") and the existing ossie export returns it on FileExistsError from publish_new_files (src/gnd/commands/export.py:99-100). Exit 10 is EXIT_DRIFT ("assets stale / missing / modified — doctor's verdict"). The D2 risk the plan documents depends on this exact exit being stated correctly in the changelog and normative text.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the collision exit code to 11 (EXIT_COLLISION) everywhere the plan and later the OB3/OB5 specs and changelog state it, and add a criterion that the new-file collision is asserted against EXIT_COLLISION, not a literal 10.
concerns.title: Plan claims collision exit 10; the codebase's collision band is exit 11

evidence.location: Completion predicates, lines 28-31, vs D2 at line 301
evidence.observation: Predicate 1 states: "`gnd export ossie MODEL --out OUT` behaves exactly as today when no new flag is given and the model's three artifacts each fit in 10 MiB: the three files are byte-identical to the baseline for every model in the export census." But the plan's own proposal D2 (a) (line 301) makes the default write five files, and the plan itself acknowledges the consequence at line 251 ("Default change (D2 a) breaks scripts that rely on three files") and line 301 ("a default run can newly fail (collision, or Rmap refusal) where it succeeded"). Under the proposed ruling, predicate 1 as written is false for no-flag runs and the milestone could not be shown complete; it only holds qualified by --ontology-only, as the plan notes at line 146-147.

concerns.recommendation: Qualify predicate 1 with the D2 ruling, e.g. "under D2 (b), when no new flag is given …; under D2 (a), with --ontology-only", mirroring the existing cross-reference to OB3-C5.
concerns.title: Completion predicate 1 contradicts the proposed D2(a) five-file default

evidence.observation: The plan pins exit 2 for new usage refusals: "`--physical-binding FILE` together with `--ontology-only` is refused as a usage error (exit 2)" (line 149), and OB1-C4 requires the --max-output-bytes argument to be "refused at the CLI boundary when 0, negative, non-integer or above the ceiling (exit 2)". The project's usage band is EXIT_USAGE = 64 (src/gnd/exits.py:46, "EXIT_USAGE = 64") and it is actively returned for usage errors by existing commands (e.g. src/gnd/discover/service.py:491-522, src/gnd/measure/service.py:378). The plan elsewhere treats exit codes as a compatibility contract (exit 3 for refusals, the collision exit in §5), so an unjustified exit 2 for program-level value validation diverges from the house convention and from the exports' own exit vocabulary.

concerns.recommendation: Route these refusals through EXIT_USAGE (64) to match gnd.exits and the other commands, or record an explicit owner-level justification for exit 2 in the plan and carry it into the OB1/OB4 specs, the normative section and the changelog.
concerns.title: New usage-error refusals pin exit 2; GND's usage band is exit 64

response.summary: Reviewed the ossie-relational-bundle plan r1 against the baseline code it names (src/gnd/export/ossie.py, src/gnd/ossie_import.py, src/gnd/commands/export.py, src/gnd/schema/ossie/core-spec.json, src/gnd/schema/ossie/PINNED.json, src/gnd/exits.py, representation-format.md). Most section 1.2 baseline claims verify: ossie:output-size refusal exists and maps to exit 3 (EXIT_ILL_FORMED), ossie_import reads at most MAX_BYTES at lines 66/78, MAX_BYTES and MAX_MODEL_BYTES are 10 MiB, tests/test_ossie_export.py indeed has no output-size coverage, core-spec Dataset has primary_key/unique_keys, Relationship requires name/from/to/from_columns/to_columns, Field requires name/expression, custom_extensions are pervasive, and PINNED.json names only ontology.json plus the core reference. Phase dependencies are acyclic and each decision-gated phase names its ruling (OB1→D3, OB2→D1/D5, OB3→D2/D4/D6, OB4→D7/D8). Three concerns: the plan misstates the existing collision exit code as 10 (code says 11), completion predicate 1 contradicts the proposed D2(a) default, and the new usage-error exit 2 contradicts the project's EXIT_USAGE=64 band.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
Cite one concrete plan location for every concern; evidence must cite the plan file itself.

Check every observed baseline claim in plan section 1.2 against the code it names (src/gnd/export/ossie.py, src/gnd/ossie_import.py, src/gnd/commands/export.py, src/gnd/schema/ossie/core-spec.json) and report any that is false.

Check that every request of the three source issues summarized in plan section 1.1 (I1-I3) is owned by a phase criterion or an explicit decision, and that no completion predicate is unfalsifiable or untestable in this repository.
Check phase ordering and dependencies for cycles, optional work supplying mandatory prerequisites, and phases that cannot be specified until a decision is ruled.

Check the proposed Halpin Rmap semantics (section 2.3), the D2 default-output change and the physical-binding design for compatibility breaks, ambiguous rules, and hostile-input or time-bound gaps against the project's standing rules in section 0.
The draft OB1 spec at notes/phase-OB1-spec.md is context only; a concern about it must still cite the plan location it derives from.
